text:
jen: Quick sync — I'm migrating the aws provider out of modules/auth and into root so multiple modules can share it. My plan:
1) hoist provider block to root with aliasing where needed
2) update module calls with `providers = { aws = aws }`
3) run `terraform state replace-provider` or `state mv` where resource addresses change
4) regenerate .terraform.lock.hcl and commit

Any gotchas I'm missing, especially around secrets wiring (k8s secrets, vault paths) or CI plan surprises?

omar: +1 on ordering. Biggest gotchas:
- provider aliases: resources created with an aliased provider need `terraform state replace-provider` not just mv sometimes
- provider requirements in modules should not hard-pin provider configs (remove provider blocks from modules)
- if you're switching provider source (mirror/registry) the lockfile will change for platforms

lee: CI note — ensure the CI runner platform matches dev when you regen lockfile. run:
```
TF_CLI_ARGS_init='-get-plugins=false' terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_amd64
```
commit the resulting .terraform.lock.hcl. Also add a quick plan job that runs `terraform init -lockfile=readonly` so PRs fail if lockfile is out of sync.

sam: secrets:
- if modules referenced secrets by path (eg `vault_generic_secret.secret.data.password`), hoisting provider can change resource addresses? usually not, but check any `provider = aws.alias` references in templates
- for k8s: we have a kustomize overlay that expects secret names in `values.yaml`. If you rename provider or change how secrets are created, update overlays and the arg to `helm_release` or `kubernetes_secret` resources

marta: small ops checklist:
- run a dry-run on staging with `-target` to validate state moves
- run `terraform state list | grep module.auth` and inspect addresses
- update module docs with provider expectations and version constraints (eg `>= 4.0, < 5.0`)

infra-bot: PR #4821 terraform plan: succeeded — 2 warnings — see https://ci.internal/4821/plan

omar: one more thing — watch out for provider mirror configs. If you use internal mirror (registry.redwood/...), make sure module `required_providers` uses the same source or else lockfile will reference different checksums and CI will fail.

jen: awesome, thanks. I'll run the staging plan tomorrow and ping @lee and @sam for a quick 👀 if anything looks off.

lee: lgtm, ping me when the staging plan link is up.

sam: can help with k8s overlay update. ping me the branch.

jen: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
